summary: A first-person account of how the author turned to aromatherapy after a period of anxiety and overwhelm, starting on September 4, 2023. Introduced to essential oils by friend Julia Thompson and given scientific context by Dr. Amelia Richards, the author built seasonal, personalized routines with oils such as lavender, lemon, peppermint, and eucalyptus. Aromatherapy was not a cure-all, but it increased mindfulness, reconnected the author with nature, and became something to share with friends.
one_line: A personal story of using essential oils and aromatherapy to ease anxiety, build mindfulness, and create seasonal wellness routines.
key_facts: The author's turning point came on September 4, 2023, when they sat at the kitchen table feeling anxious and overwhelmed.
Julia Thompson, a certified holistic wellness practitioner and friend of the author, introduced the author to essential oils.
Aromatherapy is described as an ancient practice, dating back thousands of years, promoting health through the sense of smell and skin absorption.
Certain smells trigger olfactory signals to the brain, which can influence emotions, mood, and memory.
The author started with lavender in a bedside diffuser, which let their body unwind and slowed racing thoughts; it became an evening companion.
Lemon became the author's morning pick-me-up, and a drop of peppermint oil on the wrists refreshed concentration during long afternoons.
On a stressful day in late October, eucalyptus offered clarity during a brief meditation session; rose oil was dabbed on the neck as a personal perfume.
Dr. Amelia Richards, an integrative health figure interviewed on October 20th, said certain oils can impact the limbic system, which is involved in emotional responses.
The author used topical application, diluting oils with a carrier oil and massaging them into the skin, as a multi-sensory approach to healing.
For winter the author crafted a blend of ginger, cinnamon, and orange; for spring, a floral mix of geranium and ylang-ylang.
The author used a personal inhaler during the commute and customized massage oil blends for self-care rituals.
The author hosted small gatherings to introduce friends to aromatherapy.
The author says aromatherapy was not a panacea and did not remove all tension, but it gave an enhanced awareness of the present.
